channel.title: World
channel.description: The Washington Post World section provides information and analysis of breaking world news stories. In addition to our world news and video, Post World News offers discussions and blogs on major international news and economic issues.

item.title: Russians pull billions from banks, fearing Kremlin will seize deposits for war
item.dc:creator: Catherine Belton
item.description: Russians are withdrawing billions, causing liquidity problems for banks and undermining the Kremlin’s ability to issue bonds to finance the fight in Ukraine.

item.title: U.S. Navy destroyer lost power for 4 days in South China Sea
item.dc:creator: Tara Copp
item.description: The ship’s crew lost access last month to drinkable water, running toilets and air conditioning, as the fleet sees heavy use by the Trump administration.

item.title: Kushner, Netanyahu make little progress on advancing Gaza deal after meeting
item.dc:creator: Lior Soroka, Karen DeYoung, Joshua Yang, Mohamad El Chamaa
item.description: President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and envoy first held rare talks with Hamas’s new leader in Egypt over the weekend in his effort to advance the stalled 15-point plan.

item.title: Trump defends his move to cut back U.S.-South Korea military exercises
item.dc:creator: Cleve R. Wootson Jr.
item.description: A day after attributing the decision to a good relationship with North Korea, President Donald Trump also tied the move to South Korea’s refusal to help with the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it ‘gets in the way’
item.dc:creator: Rachel Chason
item.description: The threat came in response to a question about negotiations between Iran and Oman regarding control of the Strait of Hormuz, according to a reporter.

item.title: U.S. commander calls mental health a priority after he visits USS Lincoln
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall
item.description: Amid reports of burnout and poor conditions on the USS Abraham Lincoln, Adm. Brad Cooper acknowledged that long stretches at sea can be challenging but said some of the concerns were "old news."
